description: A terminal for Web SSH connection

summary.one_liner: kkTerminal is a web-based SSH client that runs in the browser, with built-in SFTP-style file management and an embeddable terminal widget.
summary.what_it_does: It provides a browser terminal for SSH connections, built with Xterm and a Vue frontend with a SpringBoot backend using SSHJ. The File module lets you browse, decompress, upload, download, and edit remote files, saving edits back to the server with Ctrl+S. Users can customize colors, font size, cursor style, and other preferences, and set terminal options through URL parameters. Additional features listed include command code workflows, recording and replaying terminal sessions, cross-device data sync, and Cooperate, Monitor, and Docker modules. A password can be required for access. It is deployed as a Docker container on port 3000, with Nginx reverse proxy examples for root or subpath hosting.
use_cases: access a Linux server from a web browser
embed a terminal in a third-party website
upload or download files to a remote server through the browser
self-host a web SSH client with Docker
edit remote files in a browser and save them back
how_to_run: Optionally configure an Nginx reverse proxy (root path or subpath) with WebSocket upgrade headers
notable: Embeddable terminal via an HTML snippet for third-party websites
Integrated file manager with multi-select, cut/copy/paste, and in-browser editing of remote files
Shell integration and directory-following file browsing
Zero-knowledge encryption for cloud-synced data, with temporary storage of files and keys
caveats: README disclaimer limits use to personal learning and research, and prohibits illegal use
Remote-access deployment needs Nginx WebSocket proxy configuration for subpath or root hosting
Some features (cloud sync, Docker module) are described only briefly in the README
